body.purpose: Make sure the press brake is safe and ready before the first job of the shift.
steps: Test the light curtain: pass the test rod through it and confirm the ram stops.
Inspect the punch and die for chips or cracks.
Clear the work area: no loose parts, offcuts or tools on the bed or the floor around it.
Confirm the job sheet for your first job of the shift.
quality_checks: Light curtain stops the ram on every test.
No chips or cracks on the tooling.
safety_notes: If the light curtain does not stop the ram, do not run the machine. Tell your lead.
common_mistakes: Skipping the light curtain test because the machine ran fine yesterday.
Missing small chips on the die.

body.purpose: Set up the press brake to bend BR-220 brackets (10-gauge mild steel, one 90-degree bend) without scrapping parts.
steps: Check the job sheet for BR-220.
Lock out the machine before you change any tooling.
Grab the one-inch V die and the matching punch. Look them over for chips.
Set the back gauge to the flange length on the job sheet.
Bend a test piece from the same batch of steel first.
Check the test piece with the protractor. If it comes out at 92 degrees (or anything other than 90), adjust before you run the order.
Get your first good part signed off by your lead, then run the order.
quality_checks: Test piece measures 90 degrees with the protractor.
First good part signed off by your lead.
No die marks on the parts.
safety_notes: Before you change any tooling you lock out the machine, every time, no exceptions.
Keep your hands out of the light curtain. If it trips, you stop and figure out why.
common_mistakes: Skipping the test piece. Steel from different suppliers springs back different.
Adjusting after the order runs instead of before, and scrapping twenty parts.
Running with a chipped die. A chipped die marks every part.
